blue-catfish: Fishing for a mix of blue catfish and channel catfish offers some excellent fishing opportunities in the region’s tidal rivers.
A variety of cut and scented baits work well and anglers targeting the largest blue catfish often use live bait in the form of bluegill sunfish or white perch.
Fishing for blue catfish is good in the upper Choptank River this week from approximately the Dover Bridge area up to Denton and up the Tuckahoe past the Route 328 Bridge.
channel-catfish: Fishing for a mix of blue catfish and channel catfish offers some excellent fishing opportunities in the region’s tidal rivers.
Channel catfish and white catfish will also be in the mix.
largemouth-bass: Largemouth bass will generally be patrolling the transition areas between the shallows and the deepest waters.
smallmouth-bass: Fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye is good this week in the upper Potomac River and Deep Creek Lake.
Smallmouth bass will be waiting, so small crankbaits , tubes , and jigs that resemble crayfish are good choices for lures.
At Deep Creek Lake, the grass beds are also receding, and smallmouth bass will be stationed in the mid-depth areas in the search for crayfish.
striped-bass: Upper Chesapeake Bay Anglers in the upper Bay are enjoying good fishing for striped bass this week.
There are some anglers who are still able to find a few spot for live-lining along channel edges where they can detect striped bass on depth finders.
Trolling is a viable option for some and pulling umbrella rigs or tandem bucktails behind heavy inline weights is what it takes to reach the striped bass.
walleye: Fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye is good this week in the upper Potomac River and Deep Creek Lake.
Walleye can be found along steep rocky dropoffs during the evening hours and jerkbaits and small crankbaits can be good lure choices.
white-perch: Others are using small white perch or live eels.
Anglers are finding white perch in the deeper waters of the tidal rivers and creeks this week.
Fishing with small plastic jigs on a dropper rig or as a single lure are a good choice for white perch fishing in deeper waters.
